title: Nickel-62 from first principles: a zero-parameter nuclear binding maximum in Smithian Fold Theory
description:
Read the full mathematical paper (PDF)

Nickel-62 is derived as the unique nuclear binding maximum, with zero fitted coefficients. Maria Smith’s Smithian Fold Theory fixes the maximizing composition at 28 protons and 34 neutrons before opening measured nuclear data.

This self-contained paper gives the mathematics: the generated surface share 1/5, residual asymmetry and pairing shares 1/4, exact fine-structure coefficient, concave charge enumeration, rational interval separation, and the unbounded mass-tail argument. All 25,303 possible finite candidates are retained across 4,094 masses. The native Lean 4 certificate is supported by 12,545 audited declarations with zero axiom dependencies.

The independently opened AME2020 census identifies nickel-62 as the maximum among 2,548 accepted positive composite rows. Its lower reported uncertainty endpoint exceeds every rival upper endpoint by at least 2.2897 keV per nucleon; iron-58 is the runner-up.

Contents

First-principles coefficient derivation; complete nuclear ledger; exact radius enclosure; integer and parity completeness; strict unique maximum; two-case unbounded tail; exhaustive 1,024-form construction grammar; native Lean proof correspondence; full AME2020 comparison and eight anchors.

Source and verification

Original pinned V3 derivations and V4 native proof references are included in the paper and accompanying evidence. The source and evidence archive retains the entry’s 308 receipt-bound Lean modules and its original verification records. Scientific author: Maria Smith, Ernos Labs.
